speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. The combination of pain localized to the right thumb and wrist, radiating to the elbow, worsening with infant holding (pinch grip), and relief with ice is classic for this condition, likely exacerbated by the previous fall or overuse. Given your mother's history of autoimmune joint disease, I also want to rule out inflammatory arthritis. Can you confirm if you have noticed any morning stiffness in your other joints or if your grip strength has significantly weakened?
